title: Abram's Journey

named.name: Ur
named.label: below
named.note: Ur "of the Chaldeans" (11:28, 31): the great Sumerian city by the Euphrates, excavated by Leonard Woolley in 1922–34, with its ziggurat to the moon-god Nanna and the royal tombs. Local tradition places Abraham's birthplace at Urfa (Şanlıurfa) near Haran instead, but the southern city is the usual identification.

named.name: Haran
named.label: right
named.note: A city of the moon-god Sin on the Balikh river, on the main road between Mesopotamia and Syria. Terah settled and died here (11:31–32); Abram left from here at seventy-five (12:4). Rebekah's family and Laban lived in the region (24:10; 29:4).

named.name: Shechem
named.label: right
named.note: In the pass between Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim. At "the Oak of Moreh" here the LORD first promised the land to Abram's offspring, and Abram built his first altar in Canaan (12:6–7).

named.name: Moreh
named.label: below
named.note: "The Oak of Moreh," probably "the teacher's oak," a sacred tree at Shechem (12:6; compare Deuteronomy 11:30).

named.name: Bethel
named.label: left
named.note: Abram pitched his tent "with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east" and built an altar (12:8); he came back to the same place after Egypt (13:3–4). From these heights Lot looked down on the plain of the Jordan.

named.name: Ai
named.label: right
named.note: East of Bethel. The city Joshua later took (Joshua 7–8).

named.name: Negev
named.label: below
named.note: The arid south of Canaan, from Beersheba southward: grazing land in good years, the first to suffer in a drought.

named.name: Egypt
named.label: below
named.note: In famine, people of Canaan went down to Egypt, where the Nile kept the land fed. A painting in the tomb of Khnumhotep II at Beni Hasan (about 1890 BC) shows a party of 37 "Asiatics" with their donkeys arriving in Egypt.

moves.text: Terah takes Abram, Sarai and Lot from Ur toward Canaan, but they settle in Haran
At the LORD's call Abram leaves Haran for Canaan, as far as Shechem
On to the hills between Bethel and Ai, then by stages toward the Negev
Famine: down to Egypt, where Sarai is taken into Pharaoh's palace

symbols.key: Altars Abram built: at Shechem, between Bethel and Ai, and at Mamre
Altars Abram built: at Shechem, between Bethel and Ai, and at Mamre

p: From Ur to Haran along the Euphrates is about 1,000 km, and from Haran to Shechem about 700 km more: months of travel at the pace of flocks. The route follows the "Fertile Crescent," the arc of watered land between the desert and the mountains, avoiding the Syrian desert.

At each stop Abram builds an altar and "calls on the name of the LORD," marking out the land he has been promised: Shechem in the north, Bethel in the centre, Hebron in the south. The same three places become centres of Israel's later history. Jewish tradition reads the journeys of the fathers as a sign for the children, ma'aseh avot siman la-banim (Ramban on 12:6): the descent to Egypt in famine and the return with wealth foreshadow Israel's own story.
